questions.question: Halogenation of alkanes proceeds through which three stages?
questions.explanation: The radical substitution mechanism has initiation, propagation, and termination stages.

questions.question: Nitration of alkanes with nitric acid is carried out at which temperature range?
questions.explanation: Nitration of alkanes occurs at 110-120 C under pressure.

questions.question: The C-H stretching vibration of alkenes appears in which infrared region?
questions.explanation: The C-H stretch of alkenes appears around 3000 to 3100 cm-1.

questions.question: Hydroboration-oxidation of alkenes uses diborane in THF followed by which reagent?
questions.explanation: Hydroboration is followed by oxidation with hydrogen peroxide in base.

questions.question: Hydration of an alkyne first produces an enol which rearranges by which process?
questions.explanation: The enol immediately rearranges to the more stable keto tautomer by tautomerization.

questions.question: Dimerization of ethyne followed by HCl addition gives which industrial compound?
questions.explanation: Ethyne dimer gives but-1-en-3-yne, which with HCl forms chloroprene.

questions.question: Classification of alkyl halides based on the number of halogen atoms includes which term?
questions.explanation: Polyhalides contain three or more halogen atoms in the molecule.

questions.question: The reactivity order of hydrogen halides with alcohols is which?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen iodide is the most reactive and hydrogen chloride the least.

questions.question: Polar aprotic solvents used in substitution reactions include which solvent?
questions.explanation: DMSO, DMF, and acetonitrile are polar aprotic solvents.

questions.question: In SN1 reactions, a hydride shift converts which species?
options: A primary carbocation to a secondary one
A secondary carbocation to a primary one
questions.explanation: Hydride shifts convert less stable carbocations to more stable ones.

questions.question: Bulky bases such as potassium tert-butoxide favor which E2 product?
questions.explanation: Bulky bases favor the less substituted Hofmann product due to steric hindrance.

questions.question: Which sulfur reagent converts an alcohol into an alkyl chloride?
questions.explanation: Thionyl chloride is one of the best reagents for converting alcohols to alkyl chlorides.

questions.question: The carbon-carbon distance within a graphite layer is which value?
questions.explanation: The C-C distance in the graphite layer is 141.5 pm.

questions.question: The carbon-carbon distance in diamond is which value?
questions.explanation: Each carbon atom in diamond has four neighbours at 154.45 pm.

questions.question: C60 has carbon-carbon double bonds of which length?
questions.explanation: C60 has double bonds of 0.140 nm and single bonds of 0.146 nm.

questions.question: The classic preparation of C60 uses which method?
questions.explanation: Evaporation and recondensation of graphite by arc-discharge yields C60.

questions.question: Shungite is a metamorphosed meta-anthracite found in which country?
questions.explanation: Shungite from Shunga, Karelia, Russia contains C60 and C70.

questions.question: Direct fluorination of C60 with F2 gas under UV at 250 C yields which product?
questions.explanation: Fluorination with F2 gas and UV irradiation at 250 C gives C60F48.

questions.question: Acetic acid occurs naturally in which substance?
questions.explanation: Acetic acid is the main acid present in vinegar.

questions.question: Lactic acid occurs naturally in which substance?
questions.explanation: Lactic acid is found in sour milk.

questions.question: Propionic acid occurs naturally in which source?
questions.explanation: Propionic acid is found in milk products.

questions.question: Ethanedioic acid is commonly known by which name?
questions.explanation: Ethanedioic acid is commonly called oxalic acid.

questions.question: 4-Methylbenzoic acid is commonly known by which name?
questions.explanation: 4-Methylbenzoic acid is commonly called p-toluic acid.

questions.question: Ethanoic acid has a boiling point of 118 C while ethanol boils at which temperature?
questions.explanation: Ethanol boils at 78 C, much lower than ethanoic acid due to weaker hydrogen bonding.

questions.question: The word alkali comes from an Arabic word meaning which material?
questions.explanation: Alquili means ashes of plants from which sodium and potassium compounds were first isolated.

questions.question: Spodumene is heated to which temperature to convert it to the beta form?
questions.explanation: Spodumene is heated to about 1100 C to convert the alpha form to the beta form.

questions.question: Down's cell uses a eutectic mixture of 40 percent NaCl and 60 percent of which compound?
questions.explanation: The eutectic mixture is 40 percent NaCl and 60 percent CaCl2.

questions.question: Carnallite has which formula?
questions.explanation: Carnallite is KClMgCl2.6H2O, a natural source of potassium.

questions.question: The caesium clock is used for the international standard measurement of which quantity?
questions.explanation: The caesium atomic clock defines the second and the metre.

questions.question: Li3N stores up to what percentage by mass of hydrogen?
questions.explanation: Li3N stores up to 11.5 percent by mass of hydrogen.

questions.question: Which alkaline earth metal is extracted from the mineral beryl?
questions.explanation: Beryllium occurs naturally as the semiprecious mineral beryl.

questions.question: Magnesium is the third most abundant element dissolved in which medium?
questions.explanation: Magnesium is the third most abundant element dissolved in seawater after Na and Cl.

questions.question: Silicothermal reduction of dolomite uses which alloy?
questions.explanation: Dolomite is heated with ferrosilicon alloy under reduced pressure.

questions.question: Beryllium transmits X-rays how many times better than aluminium?
questions.explanation: Beryllium transmits X-rays 17 times better than Al and is used as window material.

questions.question: Lemery in 1675 divided compounds into vegetables, mineral, and which other source?
questions.explanation: Lemery divided compounds into three sources: vegetables, mineral, and animal.

questions.question: Berzelius thought organic compounds were products of which force?
questions.explanation: Berzelius proposed the vital force theory regarding carbon compounds.

questions.question: Wohler synthesized urea from ammonium sulphate and which compound?
questions.explanation: Ammonium sulphate reacts with potassium cyanate to give ammonium cyanate, which rearranges to urea.

questions.question: Kolbe synthesized acetic acid from which starting material?
questions.explanation: Kolbe synthesized acetic acid from the elements, showing organic compounds could be made chemically.

questions.question: Berthelot is credited with synthesizing which compound?
questions.explanation: Berthelot synthesized methane from its elements.

questions.question: Kekulé proposed the concept of what in organic chemistry?
questions.explanation: Kekulé proposed the theory of tetravalent carbon and the concept of valence.

questions.question: The series of steps by which a chemical reaction occurs is called which?
questions.explanation: Reaction mechanism is the series of steps by which a chemical reaction occurs.

questions.question: A species formed in one step and used up in a subsequent step is called which?
questions.explanation: An intermediate is formed in one step and used up in a subsequent step, so it is never seen as a product.

questions.question: For the elementary step A + B + C -> products, the rate law is which?
questions.explanation: For a termolecular elementary step, the rate is dependent on all three participants.

questions.question: The reaction 2NO2 + F2 -> 2NO2F has which experimental rate law?
questions.explanation: Experiments show the rate law is k[NO2][F2], so the reaction is not elementary.

questions.question: In the Arrhenius equation, R represents which quantity?
questions.explanation: R is the gas constant in the Arrhenius equation.

questions.question: A plot of ln k versus 1/T gives a straight line with slope equal to which quantity?
questions.explanation: The slope of ln k versus 1/T equals -Ea/R.

questions.question: The oxidized sulfur dioxide using nitric oxide as catalyst is an example of which catalysis?
questions.explanation: The oxidation of sulfur dioxide using nitric oxide is an example where all species are in the gas phase.

questions.question: The substance whose reaction an enzyme catalyzes is called which?
questions.explanation: The substance whose reaction the enzyme catalyzes is called the substrate.

questions.question: Scandium occurs as which rare mineral?
questions.explanation: Thortveitite is the rare mineral of Scandium with formula (Sc,Y)2Si2O7.

questions.question: The main ore of Titanium is which mineral?
questions.explanation: Ilmenite is the main ore of Titanium.
